findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition, in `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160), takes a `UserModel` parameter, so the `services` module will not compile. It should pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are lost on the normal login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. The old code filled the WebAuthn form data when the user was NOT yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`), and `authenticate()` and `challenge(...)` now rely on this helper instead. On a fresh login the user is null, so the conditional-UI data (challenge, rpId, `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`) is no longer set. Passkey autofill and the passkey form disappear from the initial login page, and the existing tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithExternalKey` and `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` would fail. Passkeys should be available both when the user is null and when re-authenticating, so the `user != null` condition is wrong (inverted or unnecessary).

findings.title: Passkey form fill gated by the wrong condition in authenticate()
findings.body: `authenticate()` now fills the passkey form only when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, which requires a non-null user. In the same method the branch for `context.getUser() == null` (loginHint / rememberMe) previously set up WebAuthn. That path no longer does, so anonymous login pages get no passkey support. The same helper has the same problem in `challenge(context, error, field)` at line 137, so passkey data is also not restored after a failed username or password on a fresh login.

findings.title: Test comment does not match what the test configures
findings.body: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` says passkeys should not appear because 'this user does not have passkey'. The test actually disables passkeys at the realm level (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`), so it does not cover the case of a realm with passkeys enabled and a user with no passkey credential. The catch-all `catch (Exception)` around `fail(...)` is also fragile. The scenario in the comment is untested.
